title: Candidate evidence ledger and week-one activation checklist
content:
Purpose:
This combined note is a pragmatic working template for two related needs we keep iterating on: (1) a simple candidate evidence ledger that consolidates signals from interviewers into a single, lightweight view for hiring committees; and (2) a pragmatic Week 1 activation checklist for ICs and managers so we minimize ramp friction and document what actually happened.

Why this exists (short):
- Hiring decisions benefit from structured, comparable evidence rather than freeform notes scattered across calendar invites and Slack.
- New hires have the highest chance of hitting early momentum if the first week is predictable and the immediate blocking items are resolved.
- This doc is intentionally lightweight (one page per candidate / one page per hire) so it travels easily in offer threads and onboarding packets.

Section A — Candidate evidence ledger (single-page template)
Instructions: paste into the candidate folder / offer thread. Keep entries brief. Use the scoring rubric below, but capture a 1–2 line take and a single evidence line (what the interviewer actually observed).
Fields to fill (one-line each):
- Candidate: [Name] / Role: [IC/Manager/Senior...] / Requisition: [REQ-XXXX]
- Panel date: [YYYY-MM-DD] / Recruiter: [name]
- Final suggested outcome: [Hire | No Hire | Hold] (optional: compensation band)

Panel summary (per interviewer):
- Interviewer name: [X] — Role eval (score 1–5): [4] — Top signal: "Handled ambiguous system design; asked clarifying Qs; whiteboard sketch shows pragmatic constraints."
- Interviewer name: [Y] — Coding eval (score 1–5): [3] — Top signal: "Completed core algo but missed edge case; good debugging approach."
- Interviewer name: [Z] — Communication/teamfit (score 1–5): [5] — Top signal: "Concise, gave clear async communication examples; strong collaborator stories."

Aggregate guidance (auto-synthesis):
- Strengths: [bullet list, 1–3 items]
- Risks / unknowns: [bullet list, 1–3 items]
- Suggested hire level & probation focus: [e.g., hire at Senior IC with 45-day check on architecture ownership]

Quick rubric (use 1–5, 5=exceeds, 1=insufficient):
- Technical craft: correctness + depth for role (1–5)
- Problem decomposition & tradeoffs: clarity of tradeoffs (1–5)
- Execution & velocity signals: delivery examples (1–5)
- Communication & collaboration: async + cross-team (1–5)
- Domain fit (inference/infra/platform): knowledge/learnability (1–5)

Evidence example (short):
- "Technical craft 4 — wrote a compact solution using two-pass approach; pointed out O(N) memory vs streaming tradeoff; ran out of time to refactor but iterative approach is solid."

Section B — Week One activation checklist (manager + new hire view)
Purpose: ensure predictable outcomes for the hire's first 5 business days. Keep items owned with a single responsible person and a due date. Assume remote-first setup.
Core items (checkbox-style; manager owns unless noted):
- [ ] Offer packet accepted + signed (owner: recruiter) — due: Day -2
- [ ] Hardware order confirmed and ETA (owner: IT ops) — due: Day -5 or earlier if customs involved
- [ ] Access provisioned: Slack, Google Drive, Okta, internal docs, repo read (owner: IT / manager) — due: Day 0
- [ ] Email + calendar invites for Week 1 created (manager) — due: Day 0; include 30m 1:1s, onboarding lunch, first-week goals sync
- [ ] 30/60/90 draft objectives shared (manager) — due: Day 0; keep this as a living doc
- [ ] Team welcome + 20-min intro slot on team meeting scheduled (manager) — due: Day 1
- [ ] Small starter task assigned (non-critical, code review or docs) with owner + due date (manager) — due: Day 1
- [ ] Codebase orientation doc + short walkthrough scheduled (engineer buddy) — due: Day 1
- [ ] Security/KMS and sensitive-data training scheduled (compliance) — due: Day 3
- [ ] Complete internal docs: infra README, deployment steps, dev env checklist (new hire) — due: Day 5
- [ ] Set up recurring 1:1 cadence for first 90 days (manager) — due: Day 5
- [ ] Early feedback checkpoint (30 days) calendar invite placed (manager) — due: Day 5

Manager tips / lightweight playbook:
- Keep Week 1 goals visible in a single doc the new hire can link in their header.
- Start with a low-risk starter task that yields quick, reviewable feedback (docs or small bug).
- Assign a single buddy (not more than two) for immediate hands-on help — buddy gets a 1hr/week sync listed in their calendar.
- If access or hardware slips: escalate to People Ops triage channel with the prefix: [ONBOARD-ESCALATE].

Section C — Interviewer guidance (quick cheat-sheet for consistent evidence)
- Purpose-driven notes: tell candidates the purpose of each interview (e.g., "system design: evaluate tradeoff framing + ops thinking").
- Capture one clear example of behavior, then a short judgement. Avoid long narrative-only notes.
- Use the rubric numbers. If you give a 2 or lower, add a short sentence explaining the blocker.
- If you have concerns about culture fit, name the specific behavior and how it maps to Redwood values.

Sample interviewer prompts (copyable):
- System design: "Design an inference-serving pipeline that needs to support 2000 rps with 95th pct latency < 100ms. Where do you start? What are the key tradeoffs?"
- Coding: "Implement a function that merges k sorted streams while keeping memory bounded; describe time/space tradeoffs and failure modes."
- Behavioral: "Tell me about a time you disagreed with a roadmap decision; how did you handle it and what was the outcome?"

Section D — Post-offer monitoring & quick checklist for People Ops
- Confirm start date & timezone; check for visa or relocation blockers.
- Pre-boarding survey: collect hardware preference, accessibility needs, calendar constraints.
- Offer-close signals to watch: >7 days silent — recruiter pings hiring manager; >14 days silent — escalate to People Ops lead.

Notes to self / open questions (working):
- Do we standardize on a single "starter task" per requisition? Pros: consistent evaluation across hires. Cons: could be gameable. Need to discuss with Eng leads.
- Should people-ops own the buddy assignment automation? We can prototype with a Google Sheet and a simple Slack bot.
- Consider a one-click synthesis that pulls interviewer ratings and outputs the one-line aggregate summary for the ledger. Who owns this? (Recruiting-eng?)

Next steps (owner + ETA):
- Iterate this template with Recruiting & Eng leads and land on a canonical field set (Maya) — ETA: 2025-12-12
- Build a first-pass Google Form for interviewer scoring to reduce transcription load (Devon) — ETA: 2025-12-05
- Pilot with two reqs in Dec hiring cycle and collect feedback (Asha) — ETA: 2026-01-15

Revision history:
- 2025-11-15: initial draft (Maya)
- 2025-11-20: added Week 1 checklist and rubric (Devon)
- 2025-12-02: clarified owner fields + added escalation tag convention (Maya)

End of doc.
